Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-07 · Updated: 2026-09-07

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  The provider has permanently adopted protocol 2, and the integration owner  
  approved using it as the current protocol. The complete new contract is:    
                                                                              
  Protocol 2: delivery_id alone identifies a delivery across all accounts; the
  same ID under another account is another receipt of that delivery. Exactly  
  one receipt is accepted per delivery identity. Accept the receipt with the  
  latest occurred_at UTC instant; equal instants use the smallest record_id.  
  All other receipts for that identity are duplicates. Each accepted receipt  
  retains its original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload. Present       
  accepted receipts in their original input order. This identity contract     
  comes from the provider's delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account         
  attribution alone does not change that guarantee.                           
                                                                              
  Update count and summary so omitted protocol selects "2" and explicit       
  "protocol":"2" selects the same agreement. Explicit protocol "1" keeps the  
  original provider contract. Shapes are unchanged; report the actual protocol
  used. The new agreement applies to the entire supplied set regardless of    
  receipt dates. Empty sets have zero counts; one receipt has one accepted and
  zero duplicates.

Delivery identity is the pair (account_id, delivery_id); identical delivery_id values in different accounts represent separate deliveries. This follows the provider delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change identity. Exactly one receipt per identity is accepted: earliest occurred_at UTC instant, with smallest record_id breaking equal-instant ties. Accepted receipts retain their original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload and are presented in original input order. For count and summary, accepted_count is the number of distinct identity pairs and duplicate_count is total receipts minus accepted_count; winner selection cannot affect these counts. operation_argv:
Courier Relay provider protocol agreement, permanently revised by trial-llv. This existing mutable key retains its original name but describes the current agreement and supported historical version. The provider permanently adopted protocol "2", and the integration owner approved it as current (source: trial-llv). Omitted protocol selects "2"; explicit "2" selects the same contract; explicit "1" remains supported. This applies to the entire supplied receipt set regardless of receipt dates.

Protocol "2": delivery_id alone identifies a delivery across all accounts; the same delivery_id under another account is another receipt of that delivery. Exactly one receipt is accepted per identity: latest occurred_at UTC instant, then smallest record_id for equal instants. This identity follows the provider delivery-ID allocation guarantee; account attribution alone does not change it.

Protocol "1" (source: vendor/protocol-1.md as recorded during trial-tbx): identity is (account_id, delivery_id), so the same delivery_id in different accounts represents separate deliveries. Exactly one receipt is accepted per identity: earliest occurred_at UTC instant, then smallest record_id for equal instants.

Both protocols compare timestamps as UTC instants, including offset date-boundary crossings; record_id order is Unicode code-point order. Accepted receipts retain original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload, and appear in original input order. For count and summary, return exactly protocol (the actual version string), accepted_count (distinct identities), and duplicate_count (total receipts minus accepted_count). Winner selection cannot affect these counts, so the current count-only implementation need not select receipt winners. Empty sets yield zero counts; singleton sets yield one accepted and zero duplicates. Requests are independent, without persistence. Ping and unknown-command responses remain unchanged.

Verified for trial-llv: all six supplied count_1/summary_1/summary_2 cases and unittest discovery passed. Regression coverage checks both commands with omitted/"1"/"2" protocol, empty/singleton/cross-account batches spanning 2020–2099, exact response shape, and unknown-command behavior; smoke covers ping. These checks verify counts, not winner selection. The actual earlier record, including historical verification when omitted protocol selected "1", is preserved at courier-relay/protocol-1/history/pre-protocol-2.
